literal: If her curved eyebrows, without bending, hide them, indeed this woman's eyes will not cause trembling grief.
translation: If her curved eyebrows would screen her eyes without bending, then surely this woman's eyes would not inflict this trembling distress upon me.
modern: வளைந்த புருவங்கள் கோணாமல் அவளுடைய கண்களை மறைத்துக் காக்குமானால், இவளுடைய கண்கள் எனக்கு நடுங்கும் துன்பத்தைச் செய்ய மாட்டா.
explanation: The speaker is overwhelmed by the beauty of the woman's eyes, which cause him a trembling distress. He imagines her curved eyebrows as guards; if they do not bend or deviate from their protective duty and instead completely screen her eyes, those eyes would not be able to look at him and cause such grief. The word 'kōṭā' means 'not bending' or 'not deviating', suggesting that the eyebrows must stand firm to shield him from the power of her gaze. Thus, the couplet uses the imagery of eyebrows acting as a barrier to the painful yet captivating power of her eyes.
